[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Using Git with Python Projects: A Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial demonstrates how to use Git, specifically with GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket, for version control in your Python projects. We'll cover essential Git commands and workflows."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Git installed on your system. Download from [https://git-scm.com/downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket account."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic knowledge of Python."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting up a Git Repository"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, create a new directory for your Python project and navigate into it using the command line."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"mkdir my_python_project
cd my_python_project"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Initialize a Git repository in the project directory."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"git init"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Python Project"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a simple Python file, for example, 'main.py', and add some code."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# main.py

def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(greet("World"))"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Adding and Committing Changes"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add the 'main.py' file to the staging area."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"git add main.py"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Commit the changes with a descriptive message."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"git commit -m "Initial commit: Added main.py""},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Repository on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Go to your chosen platform (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) and create a new repository. Choose a name for your repository and initialize it without a README, license, or .gitignore file. Copy the repository's URL."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Connecting Local Repository to Remote Repository"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add the remote repository to your local Git repository. Replace '<repository_url>' with the URL you copied."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"git remote add origin <repository_url>"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Push your local commits to the remote repository."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"git push -u origin main"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"The '-u' option sets the upstream branch, so you can use 'git push' and 'git pull' without specifying the branch in the future."},{"order":28,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a .gitignore File"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a '.gitignore' file to exclude files and directories that should not be tracked by Git (e.g., virtual environment directories, temporary files). Create a file named '.gitignore' in the root of your project."},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"# .gitignore

__pycache__/
*.pyc
venv/
.env"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add and commit the '.gitignore' file."},{"order":32,"type":"code","text":"git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Added .gitignore file""},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Branching and Merging"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a new branch for feature development."},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"git checkout -b feature/new-feature"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Make changes, add, and commit them to the feature branch."},{"order":37,"type":"code","text":"git add .
git commit -m "Implemented new feature""},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Push the feature branch to the remote repository."},{"order":39,"type":"code","text":"git push origin feature/new-feature"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a pull request on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket to merge the feature branch into the main branch. After the pull request is reviewed and approved, merge the changes."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"After merging, you can delete the feature branch locally and remotely."},{"order":42,"type":"code","text":"git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feature/new-feature
git push origin --delete feature/new-feature"},{"order":43,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":44,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covered the basics of using Git with Python projects. By following these steps, you can effectively manage your code, collaborate with others, and track changes using GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket."}]
